title: Weyl Chirality and Kitaev Topology through Bargmann Invariants
abstract: We apply a finite-state geometric formulation based on Bargmann invariants to a two-band Weyl Hamiltonian and the one-dimensional Kitaev model of a p-wave superconductor. For the Weyl system, a symmetry-antisymmetrized third-order Bargmann combination selects the chirality-sensitive component of the local pseudospin geometry and extends to a two-band lattice Weyl model. For the Kitaev chain, a normalized ratio involving a third-order Bargmann invariant and a second-order overlap factor removes the dependence on an intermediate state and reproduces the $Z_2$ distinction between its two gapped phases. We further construct a fourth-order loop connecting localized Majorana edge-mode profiles with finite-energy BdG states and an alternating fourth-order loop involving opposite Weyl pseudospin sectors. These constructions illustrate how suitable Bargmann combinations can probe chirality-sensitive, topological, and higher-order geometric information directly through quantum-state overlaps, providing an alternative state-based route without requiring a continuous description of the underlying state-space geometry.
summary: This work introduces a novel geometric framework using Bargmann invariants to characterize topological properties in condensed matter models like the Weyl and Kitaev systems. By analyzing finite-state overlaps rather than continuous geometry, the authors successfully extract chirality and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariants. This offers a robust, state-based alternative for probing complex topological physics.
main_problem: To develop a finite-state geometric formulation using Bargmann invariants to probe chirality-sensitive and topological information in quantum systems, bypassing continuous state-space descriptions.
main_result: The method successfully translates topological invariants (like chirality and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ distinction) into rephasing-invariant, finite-state overlap formulations for both Weyl and Kitaev models.
method: The core method involves constructing and analyzing higher-order Bargmann invariants (third- and fourth-order) derived from overlaps between selected quantum states.
model_or_system: The analysis applies to the two-band Weyl Hamiltonian and the one-dimensional Kitaev model of a p-wave superconductor, extending to open boundary conditions.
key_observables: Chirality-sensitive component of the local pseudospin geometry, $\mathbb{Z}_2$ distinction between gapped phases, and higher-order geometric relations involving Majorana edge modes.
important_parameters: The third-order invariant is key for chirality; the ratio of third-order to second-order invariants distinguishes the Kitaev phases.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that the relevant topological and geometric information can be captured by finite-order, state-overlap invariants rather than continuous derivatives.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first applying the third-order invariant to the Weyl system to isolate chirality, then applying it to the Kitaev chain to find the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant, and finally extending the framework to construct fourth-order loops connecting edge modes and bulk states.
why_interesting: The technique provides a powerful, purely state-based geometric tool to characterize topological phases in condensed matter systems, which is valuable for understanding boundary physics and topological invariants without relying on momentum-space continuum assumptions.
